title: Business Intern - CC
description: About Stable Money Stable Money is India’s leading fixed investment platform. It is a marketplace which helps customers discover and invest in high-quality fixed-income products such as Fixed Deposits (FDs), RD, Bonds, Credit Cards, Mutual Funds from trusted institutions. Stable Money has 30 lac+ trusted investors, 4000cr+ bookings since inception and is backed by marquee investors such as Z47, Lightspeed, Fundamentum, Matrix Partners, RTP Global to name a few. About The Category Credit Cards is a young category at Stable Money. The funnel, the partner integrations, the positioning and the customer messaging are all actively being built. That means the work is real and the surface area is large — you'll own initiatives, not fragments of work pieces. What you'll own Take an initiative from problem statement to shipped outcome — scoping, writing the spec, working with design/eng/partner teams, QA, launch, and reading the numbers after. Dig into funnel and product data to find where things are breaking, form a hypothesis about why, design the fix, and measure whether it worked. Go deep on the category: competitor cards, reward structures, partner bank policies, eligibility logic, regulatory constraints. Become the person the team asks. Talk to users and to support/sales. Bring back what's actually breaking, not what we assume is breaking. What we're looking for Generalist instinct. The work is a mix of data analysis, product thinking, and implementation — often in the same day. You should be comfortable switching between digging into numbers, thinking through a user flow, and pushing something to completion, without needing the boundaries drawn for you. Metrics understanding. A working grasp of how a business and a product are measured — funnels and conversion, retention and repeat behaviour, acquisition cost, ticket size. You should be able to look at a set of numbers and say what looks healthy, what looks broken, and what's just noise. Data-driven decisions. Before proposing a fix, you check whether the problem is real and how big it is. You quantify before you conclude — you don't argue from anecdote when a number is available, and you don't lean on a number when it doesn't actually say what you're claiming. First-principles thinking. When something is broken, you reason from the mechanism up rather than copying what a competitor did. Ownership by default. title: Solutions Engineer
description:
About the role

This role is a strong fit for data engineers with 2 to 4 years of experience who want to take their technical depth into a customer-facing role. If you have spent the last few years building pipelines, working with cloud warehouses, and solving real data problems, but you are starting to wonder what comes next, this is worth a closer look.

In this role, you will work directly with Heads of Data, Data Engineering Managers, and CTOs at companies evaluating Hevo across the US, Europe, Southeast Asia, and ANZ. You will help them design the right data architecture, walk them through trade-offs, and earn the technical trust that turns an evaluation into a partnership. You will do this independently, often as the sole technical person on the call. There is no senior SE in the background. You need to walk into a Zoom with a VP of Data Engineering at a US fintech or a Head of Analytics at a European e-commerce company, earn their technical respect in the first five minutes, and hold it for the rest of the engagement.

The technical depth you have built does not go away. It gets applied to a much wider set of problems, a much larger audience, and a global stage.

Hevo runs real-time data pipelines from 150+ sources into modern warehouses for over 1,000 companies, including DoorDash and Shopify. You will be the person customers rely on to make sure Hevo fits their stack, their scale, and their goals.


Why this role is worth considering

A. You move from building pipelines to shaping data strategy

In your current role, you build what is specified. In this role, you sit with senior data leaders and help them decide what to build across the modern data stack. Your existing experience in CDC, warehouse design, and pipeline reliability becomes the foundation for higher-leverage work.

B. You get global exposure that is hard to find elsewhere

You will be in regular technical conversations with Heads of Data and CTOs at fast-growing companies across North America, Europe, and beyond. You will run discovery, defend architecture choices, and present in rooms where decisions get made. This is rare exposure for someone at the 2 to 4 year mark, and almost unheard of from Bangalore.

C. Your technical depth stays central

This is not a pivot away from engineering. Everything you know about Postgres, CDC, Kafka, dbt, Snowflake, and pipeline reliability gets used every day. The difference is that your technical opinion shapes the customer’s architecture instead of staying inside a Jira ticket.

D. The career path is real

Strong performers in this role grow into senior individual contributor roles, lead the function, or move into product, customer success leadership, or founding-engineer roles at their next company. The optionality this role builds is significant.

What you will do

Run technical discovery calls with Heads of Data, Data Engineering Managers, and CTOs to understand their stack, pain points, and constraints. These are global conversations, primarily with customers in North America and Europe, and you will own them end to end.
Design and present reference architectures showing how Hevo fits into their existing data stack (e.g., Salesforce, Postgres, GA4, Snowflake, dbt).
Run live product demos tailored to the customer’s stack. These are not scripted walkthroughs. You will need to read the room, adapt on the fly, and handle unexpected technical questions with confidence.
Own the technical evaluation from first conversation to closed deal by addressing deep technical questions and earning trust with engineering teams.
Build proofs-of-concept by configuring real pipelines from source systems (Salesforce, Outreach, Postgres, MySQL) into destinations like Snowflake or BigQuery.
Develop deep expertise in the data integration landscape, including native solutions from AWS, GCP, and Azure (AWS Glue, Azure Data Factory, Google Cloud Dataflow) as well as other data pipeline and integration platforms, and articulate Hevo’s technical advantages in a way that lands with both technical and non-technical buyers.
Partner with Account Executives to drive technical wins, and with Customer Success to ensure smooth handoffs after a deal closes.
Share customer feedback and patterns with Product and Engineering to influence the roadmap.

What we are looking for

Must-haves

2 to 4 years of hands-on experience as a data engineer, analytics engineer, ETL/ELT developer, or data warehouse engineer.
Experience building and operating real data pipelines in production, including handling source schema changes, failures, and reliability issues.
Strong fundamentals in SQL and at least one cloud data warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery, or Redshift).
Experience with at least one orchestration or transformation tool (Airflow, dbt, or similar).
Exceptional communication and presentation skills. This is non-negotiable. You will be the face of Hevo’s technical capability to a global customer base. That means:
Your spoken English is clear, confident, and easy to follow for an international audience. You are comfortable presenting to groups of 5 to 15 people, including senior technical leaders, over video calls. You can structure a technical narrative, not just answer questions but guide a conversation toward the right conclusion. You can hold your own when a customer pushes back or challenges your recommendation. You have presented or demo’d something technical to an audience before, in any context: internal reviews, client calls, meetups, or conferences.
Genuine interest in customer-facing work, even if you have not done it formally before.

Good to have

Experience with CDC tools or data integration platforms, whether cloud-native (AWS Glue, Azure Data Factory, Google Cloud Dataflow) or third-party pipeline and integration tools.
Exposure to multiple source system types such as CRMs, ad platforms, SaaS APIs, and OLTP databases.
Public technical writing, conference talks, or open-source contributions.
Prior experience in customer conversations, even informally. For example, presenting to internal stakeholders, analytics teams, or working with international teams across time zones.

description:
About Paytm
Paytm is India's leading mobile payments and financial services distribution company. Pioneer of the mobile QR payments revolution in India, Paytm builds technologies that help small businesses with payments and commerce.

Paytm's mission is to serve half a billion Indians and bring them to the mainstream economy with the help of technology.

About the Role
Paytm is looking for an energetic, data-driven, and high-impact IT Recruiter to join our Talent Acquisition team in Noida. In this role, you will own the end-to-end recruitment lifecycle for engineering and technology roles across Paytm's core business units.
You will partner closely with Engineering Managers, Tech Leads, and HR Business Partners to source, attract, and hire high-caliber technical talent in a fast-paced, high-growth fintech environment. This role matters directly to Paytm’s growth engine: speed of technical execution starts with bringing in top-tier engineering talent who demonstrate strong ownership, business impact, and learning agility.

Key Responsibilities
End-to-End Talent Acquisition: Drive the full recruitment lifecycle for software engineering, backend, frontend, infrastructure, data, and mobile engineering roles.
Proactive Sourcing & Pipeline Building: Utilize advanced sourcing techniques (LinkedIn Recruiter, GitHub, tech communities, employee referrals, and specialized job portals) to build a robust candidate pipeline for critical engineering demands.
Hiring Manager Partnership: Collaborate with Engineering Leadership to understand technical requirements, define candidate personas, and align on hiring timelines and assessment criteria.
Candidate Experience: Ensure a transparent, engaging, and professional candidate journey from initial outreach through technical rounds to offer acceptance and onboarding.
Offer Management & Negotiation: Conduct salary fitment assessments, negotiate offer packages, and manage post-offer engagement to ensure high offer conversion rates and low drop-outs.
Process & SLA Adherence: Track key recruitment metrics including time-to-fill, cost-per-hire, channel mix, and pass-through ratios to continuously optimize hiring efficiency.

Required Qualifications
2–4 years of core hands-on experience in IT/Technical recruitment within a fast-paced Internet, Fintech, Product, or High-Growth Tech ecosystem.
Demonstrated track record of closing niche and complex engineering roles (e.g., Java, Microservices, React, Node.js, Cloud/DevOps, Data Engineering).
Strong understanding of modern technology stacks, engineering designations, and technical skill matrices.
Excellent candidate assessment, stakeholder management, and salary negotiation skills.
Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience recruiting within product-based tech companies or fast-scaling fintech startups.
Familiarity with Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) like Lever, Greenhouse, or Darwinbox.
Proven exposure to high-volume recruitment drives, hackathons, and tech community engagement.

AI Expectations
AI-Enabled Recruitment Workflows: Utilize AI tools for job description generation, candidate matching, Boolean string building, and intelligent resume parsing.
Market Intelligence & Outreach: Use AI tools for market mapping, competitive talent research, and personalizing candidate outreach emails at scale.
Productivity Improvement: Leverage AI-driven scheduling tools, automated interview updates, and automated reporting to reduce recruitment cycle times.

Ideal Candidate
Demonstrates high ownership, bias for action, and a result-oriented approach to closing open mandates.
Possesses strong learning agility and keeps pace with evolving technology trends and tech-hiring practices.
Brings a young, dynamic, and modern mindset, adapting rapidly to shifting business priorities.
Values candidate experience, diversity, and candidate-first communication.

Experience
Experience: 2–4 years

here’s what will be in store for you at CRED once you join as a part of the datascience fraud team:

role overview
as a fraud analyst at CRED, you’ll work at the intersection of data, technology and fraud prevention to identify and prevent emerging fraud patterns across products.
fraud patterns continue to evolve, making it important to identify and address emerging risks and vulnerabilities. you’ll think like an adversary -analyse data and system behaviour, spot unusual patterns and vulnerabilities, and work closely with data science, product and engineering teams to build practical solutions that prevent fraud.
this is a hands-on problem-solving role. you don’t need to be a fraud expert or a deep ml specialist. what matters is strong analytical and coding fundamentals, curiosity, and the ability to approach problems from first principles.


how is life at CRED?
 
working at CRED would instantly make you realize one thing: you are working with the best talent around you. not just in the role you occupy, but everywhere you go. talk to someone around you; most likely you will be talking to a singer, standup comic, artist, writer, an athlete, maybe a magician. at CRED people always have talent up their sleeves. With the right company, even conversations can be rejuvenating. at CRED, we guarantee a good company.
 
hard truths: pushing oneself comes with the role. and we realize pushing oneself is hard work. which is why CRED is in the continuous process of building an environment that helps the team rejuvenate oneself: included but not limited to a stacked, in-house pantry, with lunch and dinner provided for all the team members, paid sick leaves and a comprehensive health insurance. 
 
to make things smoother and to make sure you spend time and energy only on the most important things,  CRED strives to make every process transparent: there are no work timings because we do not believe in archaic methods of calculating productivity, your work should speak for you. there are no job designations because you will be expected to hold down roles that cannot be described in one word. 
 
there are many more such eccentricities that make CRED what it is but that’s for one to discover. if you feel at home reading this, get in touch.

title: Frontend Intern
description: About TrueFoundry Every production AI system whether it's powering customer support, writing code, analyzing financial data, or diagnosing medical conditions needs the same foundational infrastructure.A way to route between models. A way to manage tools and integrate them securely. A way to orchestrate agents and enforce governance. A unified compute layer to run it all. That infrastructure layer is being built right now. We're TrueFoundry, and we're building it. We're looking for a Frontend Intern to join our Enginerring team. The Problem We're Solving Companies are moving beyond simple chatbots to production agentic systems. These systems route between OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and self-hosted models. They integrate dozens of tools via protocols like MCP. They orchestrate multi-agent workflows where agents coordinate with other agents. The infrastructure to support this doesn't exist yet. You can't just duct-tape together a few API calls and call it production-ready. You need a control plane that handles: Intelligent routing with observability, cost policies, and fallback logic Centralized tool and MCP server management with security and lifecycle controls Agent orchestration with governance and guardrails A unified compute layer to run self-hosted models, custom tools, and agents We've built two products to solve this: AI Gateway is the control plane five composable components (Prompts, LLM Gateway, MCP Gateway, Guardrails, Agent Gateway) that handle routing, orchestration, and governance. AI Deploy is the compute layer of Kubernetes-based platform that abstracts ML workloads as standard software primitives, so everything runs on unified infrastructure. We're Series A, backed by Intel Capital and Sequoia. Companies like CVS, Mastercard, Siemens, Paytm, Synopsys, and Zscaler run production AI workloads on our platform. Role Overview We are looking for Frontend Engineering Interns who are excited about building developer-focused products and modern web applications. You will work closely with our product and engineering teams to craft intuitive, high-performance user interfaces for AI/ML platforms used by developers and enterprises globally. This is a hands-on role where you will ship real features to production. What You’ll Do Build and improve frontend features for TrueFoundry’s core platform Develop responsive, high-quality UI using modern frontend frameworks Collaborate with backend, design, and product teams to ship end-to-end features Optimize performance, usability, and scalability of the frontend Work on dashboards, developer tools, and AI workflow interfaces Write clean, maintainable, and reusable code Participate in code reviews and engineering discussions Tech Stack Languages/Frameworks: JavaScript, TypeScript, React.js, Next.js Styling: TailwindCSS / CSS / Component libraries Tools: Git, GitHub, REST APIs, modern build tools Good to know: Basic understanding of AI/ML platforms or developer tools (not mandatory) Who You Are Pursuing B.E/B.Tech in Computer Science Strong fundamentals in HTML, CSS, JavaScript Familiarity with React.js or modern frontend frameworks Understanding of APIs and web application architecture Eye for UI/UX and detail-oriented development Strong problem-solving and learning mindset Ability to work in a fast-paced startup environment

title: Research Intern - AI Evaluations
description: About Karya : Why was Karya on the cover of the Time Magazine , highlighted by Satya Nadella , and chosen by Google as its partner for Project Vaani ? You'll be expected to stay current on AI evaluation science itself, and use your disciplinary training to ask sharper questions about what these systems are actually doing, and to whom. Concretely, this means: Applying social science research methods (qualitative and/or quantitative) to the evaluation of AI/ML systems, particularly language technologies Contribute to developing AI evaluation and testing methodologies Investigating how these technologies interact with and affect the communities they're deployed among, especially in rural and low-resource contexts in India Working closely with the Evaluations team to understand both the "build" and "evaluate" sides of AI systems This role is well suited to someone who's curious about tech and wants to put their social science training into practice. You'll be working alongside engineers, bringing a rigorous footing and a social science researcher's lens into a technical space. If you're a social science student or researcher who's been eyeing the AI/tech space and wondering how to get in, this is that entry point. You'll work on live evaluation pipelines, with communities across India, on low- and high-resource language technologies, alongside a team that treats social science expertise as core to the work. Qualifications Education Currently pursuing or recently completed an undergraduate or master's degree in a social science discipline (Sociology, Anthropology, Development Studies, Gender Studies, Political Science, Economics, or Science and Technology Studies (STS) No technical degree required, but demonstrated interest in and conceptual understanding of AI/ML systems is expected. E.g., through self-directed learning, coursework, or prior projects at the intersection of technology and society Skills and Competencies Strong grounding in social science research methods qualitative, quantitative, or mixed (not a hard requirement, but research training expected) Comfort conducting or supporting focus group discussions (FGDs) and field visits Conceptual understanding of AI/ML systems - applied AI/ML literacy - enough to engage meaningfully with concepts like model evaluation, human-in-the-loop systems, and language technologies (you don't need to code, but you should be comfortable with how these systems are built and tested) Familiarity with socio-technical systems thinking (i.e., understanding technology and society as mutually shaping, not separate concerns) Multilingual proficiency in Indian languages is a strong plus Background in computational social science is a plus, not a requirement Strong written and verbal communication skills Comfort working in ambiguous, early-stage research settings People matter at Karya and these are some of the perks and benefits we created for our team: • Flexible vacation and leave policy • Flexible work options • Insurance as per industry standards • Access to industry stalwarts and networking opportunities Karya is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer. Functional QC & Test Recording Power up each rig and confirm cameras open, storage is available, and the device is charged/charging correctly Capture a short test recording and review it: cameras correctly aligned, footage clear and stable, audio present, timestamps correct Confirm the SD card reads correctly, the previous session's data has been offloaded, and the card is cleared and ready for reuse Only mark a rig "field-ready" once every check passes 3. Outbound Approval (clearing rigs for field) Give the final go/no-go before a rig is handed to a Field Officer Ensure the rig leaves fully charged, correctly configured, and with the right accessories Sign off in the tracker so every field-ready rig is traceable to your check 4. Instawork Robotics Lab (IRL) Robots are getting smarter, but they still can’t reliably do the everyday physical tasks people do — chopping vegetables, stocking shelves, assembling parts. The bottleneck is data. UC Berkeley’s Prof. Ken Goldberg calls it the “100,000-year data gap”: the chasm between the massive text datasets used to train language models and the tiny amount of real-world, physical-dexterity data available to train robots. The entire robotics industry collected only ~100,000 hours of training data in 2024 and ~1 million in 2025 — and even the ~20 million hours projected for 2026 is still less than 0.04% of what is ultimately needed. IRL exists to close that gap. Workday operations Monitor the Workday inbox for business process errors, stuck transactions, alerts, and other operational issues. Complete routine Workday support tasks, including standard access requests, account maintenance, and operational follow-up. Support Salesforce and JIRA run work and respond to common People Systems questions using approved guidance. Help with recurring operational tasks such as account monitoring, account resets, and quarterly account reviews. Support year-end activity, including schedule extensions, alert configuration, audit requests, and tracking follow-up items. Reporting, documentation, and Jira support Intake and triage Workday reporting and data requests. title: Software Engineer, New Grad
description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible. Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works. Small teams can impact how millions of businesses grow. Right now the global economy is replatforming around AI, creating new opportunities for growth. We believe new programming languages can be learned if the fundamentals and general knowledge are present. Experience from either previous internships or working collaboratively on multi-person coding projects (in a university or professional setting). Ability to learn unfamiliar systems and form an understanding of those systems, through independent research and working with a mentor or subject matter experts. Clear written communication skills, with the ability to explain your work to stakeholders, team members, and other Stripes. Ability to leverage AI tools to accelerate development while applying rigorous critical thinking and professional judgement to review, refine, and validate all outputs. Preferred qualifications One or more areas of specialized knowledge (frontend, backend, infrastructure or other technologies) balanced with general skills and knowledge. Experience in code review practices, and an understanding of how to safely update production systems. Familiarity with navigating and managing work in large code bases. Experience leading small projects independently, and contributing to larger projects alongside peers. Ability to operate with high agency in navigating complex technical obstacles independently, knowing precisely when to unblock oneself and when to ask for help.

We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible. Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works. You’ll own problems end to end with the support of your manager and teammates. It’s an opportunity to work alongside some of the most creative and technically rigorous engineers in the industry and learn how to ship high-quality work at scale. By contributing to Stripe’s codebase you’ll work across domains that give you insight into how the global economy works. Recent intern projects include expanding Stripe’s Payments Foundation Model capabilities to improve generalized anomaly detection, building more approachable fraud controls, creating safer payouts, and developing user-facing solutions that prevent costly pricing mistakes and make merchant checkout setup easier. At Stripe we embrace kindness while encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus. Experience and familiarity with programming, either through side projects or classwork. We work mostly in Ruby, Java, Javascript, Go, and Scala. Experience from previous internships or other multi-person projects, including open source contributions, that demonstrate evaluating and receiving feedback from mentors, peers, and stakeholders. Familiarity with navigating and managing your work in new code bases, with multiple languages. Clear written communication skills, with the ability to write clearly to explain your work to stakeholders, team members, and other Stripes.

title: Embedded Data Scientist, Chanakya
description: About Sarvam Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India's full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC. About the Role Embedded Data Scientists transform complex client data into structures that AI systems can reliably reason over. You are deployed alongside Strategic Deployment Engineers at client sites, working directly with client data environments to understand, structure, and operationalise large-scale datasets. This means working with heterogeneous, multimodal data — including documents, images, audio, geospatial data, and structured records — and designing the semantic structures that allow AI systems to interpret and reason over that data. You will define how data is represented inside the AI system: how documents are segmented, how metadata is defined, how entities and relationships are represented, and how different data modalities connect. You will design ontologies, tagging systems, and knowledge graph structures that allow the reasoning engine to operate effectively. title: Product User Research, Intern
description: About Sarvam AI Sarvam AI is building India's sovereign AI stack, spanning foundational models, infrastructure and applications. Our mission is to make powerful AI accessible and useful for India, building technology that works across languages, industries and real-world use cases. As we continue to build and scale our products, understanding how people interact with them becomes increasingly important. We're looking for a curious and research-oriented intern to help us understand our users better and shape the experiences we build. The Role As a Product User Research Intern, you'll work closely with our product, design and engineering teams to understand user behaviour, identify friction points and uncover opportunities to improve our products. You'll interact directly with developers, product managers and founders, study how they use Sarvam's products, and translate your findings into actionable insights that influence product and design decisions. This is an opportunity to work on a new user research function at Sarvam, helping establish research practices and processes from the ground up. You'll also get ownership of a primary product area and the opportunity to see your research translate into real product improvements. What You'll Work On Understand our users: Conduct user interviews, surveys and usability studies with developers, PMs and founders to understand their needs, behaviours and challenges. Improve product experiences: Research user journeys across Sarvam's developer console, playground, API documentation and applications. Identify friction points across onboarding, API key creation, first API calls, billing and other key workflows. Study developer journeys: Analyse the developer funnel, from sign-up to making the first API call and eventually becoming a paying user. Understand where users drop off and, more importantly, why. Test and evaluate designs: Conduct usability testing on existing interfaces and new prototypes, run preference and A/B tests, and benchmark experiences against other developer products. Turn research into insights: Analyse qualitative and quantitative data, identify patterns and present clear recommendations to product, design, growth and support teams. Build the research practice: Help establish research playbooks, interview templates, participant recruitment processes and a research repository that can scale with the team. What We're Looking For Strong curiosity about user behaviour and a genuine interest in understanding why people use products the way they do. Comfortable speaking with users, conducting interviews and asking thoughtful, unbiased questions. Technical fluency — you should be comfortable reading API documentation, making basic API calls using tools like Postman, curl or Python, and understanding what might have gone wrong when an API fails. Comfortable working with data, analysing spreadsheets and interpreting product funnels or dashboards. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate research findings into clear insights and recommendations. Familiarity with AI tools and developer products, and an interest in exploring how they can improve research workflows. Good to Have Experience with SQL or product analytics tools such as Mixpanel, Amplitude or Metabase. Familiarity with user research methodologies, usability testing and survey design. Experience reviewing Figma prototypes or conducting user interviews. Previous research projects, internships or personal projects involving products you've built or shipped. Fluency in one or more Indian languages. Who Can Apply? Final-year students or graduates who have completed their studies within the last 12 months. Candidates from engineering, psychology, economics, design or social science backgrounds. Individuals who can commit to a full-time, 6-month, in-office internship in Bengaluru. What You'll Get The opportunity to help build Sarvam's user research function from the ground up. Direct exposure to product, design and engineering teams working on India's sovereign AI ecosystem. Hands-on experience researching developer products and real-world AI applications. Ownership of meaningful research projects with findings that directly influence product decisions. An opportunity to work closely with experienced product leaders and learn how research translates into better products. Potential for a pre-placement offer (PPO) based on performance.

title: Technical Writer
description: About Sarvam Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. You’ll work closely with researchers, engineers and product teams to write about the decisions, advances and practical applications behind our work. That could mean explaining how we train a model, developing the story for a product launch or showing developers how to build with our APIs. The role calls for technical curiosity and strong editorial judgement. You should enjoy getting into the details, asking questions until you understand something and finding a clear, compelling way to explain it. You’ll have substantial ownership over what we publish and how we sound. What you’ll do Write research papers, engineering blogs, product announcements and technical deep dives across Sarvam’s models and products. Work directly with researchers and engineers to understand their work, draw out interesting ideas and develop pieces from early conversations through publication. Explain technical approaches, benchmark results and design decisions with enough detail for readers to understand the evidence and trade-offs. Develop launch narratives that clearly articulate what a model or product does, what has improved and where it is useful. Adapt ideas across formats, from a detailed technical article to a product page, launch email or short social post. Edit contributions from technical teams, strengthening their structure and readability while preserving the author’s expertise and intent. Own fact checking, technical reviews and revisions, and help establish consistent editorial standards across our published work. What you’ll bring A portfolio of published work that demonstrates clear thinking, strong writing and the ability to explain technical subjects. Enough familiarity with AI and software to read technical material, follow an engineering discussion and ask informed questions. Strong judgement about structure, voice and detail. You can find the central idea in a complex subject and build a piece around it. The ability to write for developers and researchers, as well as readers encountering a subject for the first time. Care with evidence and claims. You know when a statement needs a source, a qualification or another conversation with the team. Experience working with subject experts and incorporating feedback while keeping a piece coherent. The initiative to identify stories worth telling and the discipline to bring them through to publication. Experience that would help You may have worked as a technical writer, technology journalist, developer educator or editor at a technology company or research organisation. Experience with AI models, APIs, developer tools or infrastructure would be useful, as would the ability to try products and run simple code examples yourself.
